paper_metadata.title: High temperature processing of Mg–Zn–Y alloys containing quasicrystal phase for high strength

evidence.quote: A process to obtain high strength in a Mg–Zn–Y alloy containing quasicrystalline phase is described.

samples.original_name: Mg–6 at% Zn–1 at% Y alloy

evidence.quote: An alloy with composition Mg–6 at% Zn–1 at% Y was made by melting high purity elements

An alloy with composition Mg–6 at% Zn–1 at% Y was made by melting high purity elements
An alloy with composition Mg–6 at% Zn–1 at% Y was made by melting high purity elements with a mixture of cover gases CO2 and SF6, and cast in steel molds.
The alloy was solutionized at 480 ◦C for 24 h in a muffle furnace with inert atmosphere
followed by extrusion at 430 ◦C and 380 ◦C (referred hereafter as alloy e430 and e380, respectively) with an extrusion ratio of 25:1, into 8 mm diameter rods
followed by extrusion at 430 ◦C and 380 ◦C (referred hereafter as alloy e430 and e380, respectively) with an extrusion ratio of 25:1, into 8 mm diameter rods
Stress–strain curves for the e430 extruded alloy before and after peak ageing (at 150 ◦C for 30 h) are shown in Fig. 6a.

In the e380 alloy the strengths were higher in the as-extruded condition, tensile YS about 251 MPa and compressive strength about 210 MPa. After peak ageing at 150 ◦C for 30 h, the tensile YS was 338.1 ± 6.4 and the compressive YS 246.4 ± 10.6 MPa.

attributes.composition: about 21 at% Mg, 70 at% Zn, 9 at% Y

evidence.quote: The presence of the icosahedral i-phase, the cubic W-phase and the pre-eutectic H-phase [15] was confirmed by electron diffraction patterns.
The i-phase is identified in the lamellar region B, whose composition was analyzed to be about 21 at% Mg, 70 at% Zn and 9 at% Y.

attributes.composition: ∼16 at% Mg, 60 at% Zn, 24 at% Y

evidence.quote: Position C was detected to be the H phase (∼16 at% Mg, 60 at% Zn, 24 at% Y).
The presence of the icosahedral i-phase, the cubic W-phase and the pre-eutectic H-phase [15] was confirmed by electron diffraction patterns.
In its vicinity at D, elemental yttrium phase was also detected (∼97 at% Y).
The solutionized alloy had a grain size of over 300 /H9262m, as shown in Fig. 1a.

attributes.morphology: particles, banded regions along extrusion direction

evidence.quote: A dark banded region running vertically along the extrusion direction contains submicron size i-phase particles.
A dispersion of about 50–100 nm size i-phase particles occurred in the matrix, some of which are marked by arrows in Fig. 5a.

attributes.location: matrix, irregularly spaced 100 µm or more apart

evidence.quote: In some places, very large particles of ∼20 /H9262m size are observed, some of which are indicated by arrowheads. These were determined to be the W phase. Distribution of the W-phase particles in the matrix was found to be irregular and they were spaced 100 /H9262m or more apart.
After extrusion, the average grain size was 20 ± 6 /H9262m for e430 and 13.8 ± 6 /H9262m for e380, as observed in Fig. 2a and b.
In case of e430, about 200 nm size particles occurred continuously along all the grain boundaries, while in case of e380 the i-phase particles did not occur on all the grain boundaries.
The formation of the i-phase at the grain boundaries resulted in a solute depleted zone, as evidenced in the HAADF micrograph of Fig. 5a.

attributes.size: width 7.2 ± 2.2 nm, length 25.15 ± 3.3 nm, aspect ratio 4.27 ± 1.2
attributes.morphology: rod-like, aligned parallel to hexagonal axis of matrix

evidence.quote: Ageing resulted in a very dense precipitation of rod-like /H92521′ precipitates in the matrix.

mechanisms.name: grain-boundary nucleation and precipitation of i-phase

evidence.quote: The extrusion temperature of 430 ◦C is within the temperature range of the eutectic, while 380 ◦C is below it. This may explain the formation of the i-phase particles on the grain boundaries in the e430 alloy but not much in case of the e380.
The precipitation of the i-phase will be more favorable on the grain boundaries because yttrium has very low solubility and diffusion rate in the matrix.
Due to the dense precipitation of the /H92521′ precipitate in the matrix, a very high ageing response was observed, resulting in a very high YS.
The reason for the low ductility was identified to be the large particles of W-phase (Fig. 3) which act as inclusions because of their large size.
